most_common: STATEMENT BY COMMISSIONERS R. SUSAN MOTLEY AND THEODORE E. TEAH ON LOWER EAST SIDE PUBLIC HOUSING PROJECT November 10, 1982 C831083HOM C830007HDM C830008HUM N830009HGM We abstain. We cannot in good conscience vote against desperately needed low income housing to be built on the Lower East Side. However, this project - both the process by which it was developed and several components of the end plan including the planned demolition of 53 Stanton Street - raise serious issues that have not, in our judgment, been adequately addressed. We therefore withhold our votes on this project.

' CITY PLANNING COMMISSION December 21, 1987 / Calendar No. 1 C 861180 ZMM IN THE MATTER OF an application submitted by Glenwood Management Corporation pursuant to Sections 197-c and 200 of the New York City Charter for an amendment to the Zoning Map, Section 9a, changing: 1)fromaC8-4distri.to an R8 district property bounded by a line 464 feet east of First Avenue, the former northerly street line of East 93rd Street, a line 488 feet east of First Avenue, and East 92nd Street; and 2) from a C8-4 district to an R10 district property bounded by a line 488 feet east of First Avenue, Franklin D. Roosevelt Drive, York Avenue and East 92nd Street and establishing within the proposed R10 district a C2-5 district, Borough of Manhattan, Community District 8, as shown on a diagram dated September 16, 1987. The application for a Zoning Map amendment to facilitate the development of a 36-story mixed-use, predominantly residential development located on the northwest corner of East 92nd Street and York Avenue was submitted by Glenwood Management on June 9, 1986 and revised in August, 1987. RELATED ACTION In addition to the proposed amendment of the Zoning Map, implementation of the proposed project also requires favorable action by the City Planning Commission and Board of Estimate on a related application (C 870156 ZSM), being considered concurrently with the proposed Zoning Map change, for a special permit for a 137-car public parking garage pursuant to Sections 13-462 and 74-52 of the Zoning Resolution, which is the subject of a separate report dated December 21, 1987. BACKGROUND The site is located in the Yorkville neighborhood of Community District 8. The surrounding mid-blocks are generally low-rise and residential in character, although there are clusters of high-rise residential structures and a pocket of light-industrial and automotive uses just west of the site. Most of these low-rise structures were built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
